title: “Here, venerable sir, a person has no stain but does not truly know: ‘There is no stain in me.’ For such a person, it can…
content: “Here, venerable sir, a person has no stain but does not truly know: ‘There is no stain in me.’ For such a person, it can be expected: ‘He will attend to the sign of the beautiful. By attending to the sign of the beautiful, greed will pollute his mind. He will die with greed, with ill-will, with delusion, with stain, his mind polluted.’ Venerable sir, just as a bronze bowl brought from the market or from the smithy, clean and pure, and the owner does not use it, does not wipe it, and throws it into a dusty place – that bowl, after a time, becomes more defiled and dustier.”

title: “Monks, how is a monk one who does not know forms? Here, monks, a monk does not know as it actually is all form, namely…
content: “Monks, how is a monk one who does not know forms? Here, monks, a monk does not know as it actually is all form, namely the four great elements and form derived from the four great elements. Thus, monks, a monk does not know forms. Monks, how is a monk one who is not skillful in characteristics? Here, monks, a monk does not know as it actually is the fool and the characteristics of a fool, the wise person and the characteristics of a wise person. Thus, monks, a monk is not skillful in characteristics. Monks, how is a monk one who does not remove the eggs of the gadfly? Here, monks, a monk indulges in arisen sensual thoughts; he does not abandon, dispel, end, or destroy them. He indulges in arisen ill-will thoughts … harmful thoughts … evil, unwholesome states that have arisen; he does not abandon, dispel, end, or destroy them. Thus, monks, is a monk who does not remove the eggs of the gadfly.”

title: “Vāseṭṭha, there are five factors that cause the growth of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye — desirable, beautiful, delightful, enticing, connected…
content: “Vāseṭṭha, there are five factors that cause the growth of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye — desirable, beautiful, delightful, enticing, connected with sensual pleasure and enjoyment; sounds cognizable by the ear … odors cognizable by the nose … tastes cognizable by the tongue … touches cognizable by the body — desirable, beautiful, delightful, enticing, connected with sensual pleasure and enjoyment. Vāseṭṭha, those five factors that cause the growth of sensual pleasure — the brahmins proficient in the three Vedas, attached, infatuated, bound, not seeing their danger, not understanding the escape from them, enjoy them. Vāseṭṭha, that those brahmins proficient in the three Vedas, abandoning the qualities that make a brahmin, following qualities that do not make a brahmin, attached, infatuated, bound, not seeing their danger, not understanding the escape from them, enjoying them, bound by the bondage of sensual pleasures, could after death be reborn in union with Brahmā — such a thing is not possible.”

title: “What are the five mental shackles not yet cut off? Monks, here a monk is not free from lust, desire, affection, thirst, fever, craving for…
content: “What are the five mental shackles not yet cut off? Monks, here a monk is not free from lust, desire, affection, thirst, fever, craving for sensual pleasures. Monks, for a monk who is not free from lust … craving for sensual pleasures, his mind does not incline to exertion, commitment, persistence, striving. If one’s mind does not incline to exertion, commitment, persistence, striving, this is the first mental shackle not yet cut off.”

title: Venerable Todeyya: “One in whom desires do not dwell, One in whom craving is not found, One who has crossed beyond doubt — What is…
content:
Venerable Todeyya:
“One in whom desires do not dwell,
One in whom craving is not found,
One who has crossed beyond doubt —
What is the liberation of such a one?”

The Blessed One replied to Todeyya:
“One in whom desires do not dwell,
One in whom craving is not found,
One who has crossed beyond doubt —
There is no other kind of liberation.”

Venerable Todeyya:
“Does such a one have longing,
Or is he free from longing?
Does he have wisdom,
Or is he still acquiring wisdom?
O all-seeing sage, explain this to me,
So that I may know what a sage is, O Sakyan.”

The Blessed One:
“He is free from longing,
Without any longing —
He is wise, not acquiring wisdom.
Thus, Todeyya, know the sage:
Possessing nothing,
Not attached to sensual existence.”

title: Elder Uttarapāla: I am truly virtuous, Reflecting on good purpose. I have abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure, Which are the world’s confusion. Born…
content:
Elder Uttarapāla:

I am truly virtuous,
Reflecting on good purpose.
I have abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure,
Which are the world’s confusion.

Born in Māra’s realm,
Struck by strong darts,
Yet I have escaped
Māra’s snare.

All sensual desires are destroyed,
All forms of existence are demolished.
The path of birth and death is ended —
Now there is no further becoming.

title: “Monks, it is because of not realizing, not penetrating the Four Noble Truths that you and I have wandered and wandered through this long course.…
content:
“Monks, it is because of not realizing, not penetrating the Four Noble Truths that you and I have wandered and wandered through this long course. What four? Because of not realizing, not penetrating the noble truth of suffering, monks, you and I have wandered and wandered through this long course … the noble truth of the origin of suffering … the noble truth of the cessation of suffering … Because of not realizing, not penetrating the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering, monks, you and I have wandered and wandered through this long course. But now, monks, the noble truth of suffering has been realized and penetrated. The noble truth of the origin of suffering has been realized and penetrated. The noble truth of the cessation of suffering has been realized and penetrated. The noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering has been realized and penetrated. Cut off is craving for existence; destroyed is what leads to renewed existence. Now there is no further becoming.” The Blessed One said this … the Teacher further said:

From not seeing the four noble truths
As they really are,
One wanders for a long time
Through many births.
But when these are seen,
The root of rebirth is pulled out,
The root of suffering is cut off —
Now there is no further becoming.

title: - “What do you think, Mālukyaputta? Regarding forms cognizable by the eye that you have not seen, never saw before, do not see now, and…
content:
- “What do you think, Mālukyaputta? Regarding forms cognizable by the eye that you have not seen, never saw before, do not see now, and do not wish to see — do you have any desire, lust, or craving for them?” - “No, venerable sir.” - “Regarding sounds cognizable by the ear … odors cognizable by the nose … tastes cognizable by the tongue … touches cognizable by the body that you have not felt, never felt before, do not feel now, and do not wish to feel — do you have any desire, lust, or craving for them?” - “No, venerable sir.”

Seeing a form, if one’s mind is infatuated,
Attending to a pleasing sign,
The mind is attached to the feeling,
Clinging to the form remains.
His feelings increase,
Manyfold, born from form —
Greed and hurtful thoughts
Harm his mind.
Thus accumulating suffering,
He is said to be far from Nibbāna.

Hearing a sound, mind infatuated …
Smelling an odor …
Tasting a flavor …
If one’s mind is infatuated,
Attending to a pleasing sign,
The mind attached to the feeling,
Clinging to the flavor remains.
His feelings increase,
Manyfold, born from flavor —
Greed and hurtful thoughts
Harm his mind.
Thus accumulating suffering,
He is said to be far from Nibbāna.

title: “Monks, what one intends, what one plans, and what one has a tendency towards — that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness. When…
content: “Monks, what one intends, what one plans, and what one has a tendency towards — that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is a basis, consciousness becomes established. When consciousness is established and grows, there is a leaning (nati). When there is a leaning, there is a going to a state of rebirth. When there is a going to a state of rebirth, there is future birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. Such is the origination of this whole mass of suffering. Monks, if one does not intend, does not plan, and has no tendency towards anything, there is no basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is no basis, consciousness does not become established. When consciousness is not established and does not grow, there is no leaning. When there is no leaning, there is no going to a state of rebirth. When there is no going to a state of rebirth, there is no future birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

title: “Monks, there are these five defilements of the mind because of which the mind becomes defiled, not malleable, not wieldy, not radiant, brittle, and not…
content: “Monks, there are these five defilements of the mind because of which the mind becomes defiled, not malleable, not wieldy, not radiant, brittle, and not properly concentrated for the destruction of the defilements. What five? Sensual desire, ill-will, sloth and torpor, restlessness and remorse, doubt. These five defilements of the mind, monks, because of which the mind becomes defiled, not malleable, not wieldy, not radiant, brittle, and not properly concentrated for the destruction of the defilements.”
